lawyer:
Dr. Kamal Hossain with Mr. M.K. Rahman, Advocates ------ For the Petitioners 
Mr. Md. Serajul Huq. A.A.G. ------ For the Respondents
parties:
Md. Idris Miah alias Idris Ali and others ------ Petitioners
Vs.
The State and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment:
Md. Ruhul Amin, J: Petitioners have obtained this rule under Article 102(2)(a)(ii) of the Constitution of the People's Republic of Bangladesh calling upon the respondents the State. represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Sherpur. Superintendent of Police, Sherpur. Md. Abul Hossain Mondal. Sub-Inspector of Police, Sherpur Police Station, Sherpur and Md. Nazrul Islam, Officer-in-Charge, Sherpur Police Station. Sherpur to show cause as to why the arrest of the petitioners and seizure of manually manufactured cigarattes (Biris) and the proceedings of G.R. Case No. 43(2)89 arising out of Sherpur P.S. Case No. 10 dated 25.5.1989 under Section 46 of the Excise Act pending before the Upazila Magistrate (as then was) Sherpur instituted by the respondent Nos. 3 and 4. S.I. of Police Sherpur Police station and officer in-charge of Sherpur Police station respectively should not be declared to have been made and initiated without lawful authority and is of no legal effect or such other or further order or orders passed as to this court may seem fit and proper. 

 3. That petitioner No. 1's success in the business made other persons in the similar and same business his rival and that said persons being enemical to the petitioner No. 1 were up and down to cause damage to his business: that petitioner No. 1 marketed his product by affixing bandorol of a value appropriate to the rate of duty in force at the relevant time and that paid duties regularly; that because of petitioner No. 1's popularity and success in the business and the demand of the product of the petitioner's firm made others in the business hostile to the petitioner No. 1 and thereupon the said persons in collaboration with the officials were in conspiracy to dis-credit the petitioner No. 1 and to ruin his business that on 25.5.1989 at about 3.45 a.m. respondent No. 3 with Police force illegally and in an unlawful manner seized 100 bags of manually manufactured cigarettes (Biris) from a loaded Truck and arrested the petitioner Nos. 2-8 the employees of the petitioner No. 1 and a customer of petitioner No. 1's product who was board in the Truck that Biris so detained and the persons arrested were taken to Sherpur Police station and then an F.I.R. was lodged alleging that having realised that 33 bags of Biris loaded in the seized Truck manufactured by petitioner No. Is firm were going to be sold by the apprehended persons either without Bandorol or that upon affixing old bandorols and thus was avoiding payment of Excise Duty, that on the basis of the F.I.R. so lodged by the respondent No. 3. respondent No. 4 started Sherpur P.S. Case No. 10 dated 25.5.1989 under Section 46 of the Excise Act, that on 26.5.1989 the respondent No. 3 sealed factory of the petitioner No. 1 and that also searched his house and also searched the factory of the petitioner No. 1, that the petitioner Nos. 3-8 were enlarged on bail by the Upazila Magistrate on 26.5.1989 and that petitioner No. 2 was enlarged on bail by the learned Sessions Judge Sherpur on 27.5.1989; that on 27.5.1989 Respondent No. 4 sought for the permission of the Upazila Magistrate to sell the seized 100 bags of manually-manufactured cigarettes and that on 28.5.1989 the Upazila Magistrate upon observing that there as there were procedural defect in instituting the case by the Police sent the file to the District Magistrate Sherpur for necessary order: that the District Magistrate on 28.5.1989 passed order for handing over the seized cigarettes the Excise Officer and thereupon the seized cigarettes were handed over to the Officer of Customs Department of Jamalpur; that on 6.6.1989 petitioner No. 1 surrendered before the District Magistrate, Sherpur and was enlarged on bail. Petitioners have contended that petitioner No. 1 is the manufacturer of cigarettes having licence under the Excises and Salt Rules 1944 as framed under the Escises and Salt Act 1944 and that there is no provision in the Act or the Rules authorities police to seize manually-manufactured cigarettes on the allegation of not affixing bandorols or that marketing the manually-manufactured cigarettes without duty. It has further been contended by the petitioners that for alleged offence of avoiding payment of duty in marketing manually manufactured cigarettes police is not authorised to apprehend any person: that the facts stated in the First Information Report lodged by the Respondent No. 3 on 25.5.1989 and on the basis whereof Sherpur P.S. Case No. 10 dated 25.5.1989 as has been started by respondent No. 4 as no criminal prosecution lies against the petitioners and as such the aforementioned criminal case so started against the petitioners is without lawful authority and is liable to be declared illegal: that the arrest as made by the respondent No. 3 was illegal in that for alleged non-payment of Excise duty Respondent No. 3 or any personnel of the Police under the law was not authorised to arrest a person and that as per provision of law police shall only act when assistance of police is sought by the Excise Officer and that for alleged avoidance of payment of duty only the Excise Officer is authorised under the law to arrest a person; that initiation of the proceeding by the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 for purported prosecution of the petitioners tinder Section 46 of the Excise Act is wholly unlawful arbitrary unwarranted and that continuation and prolongation of the case amounts to abuse of the process of the court causing hardship and harassment to the petitioners, that the proceeding initiated by the respondent No. 3 through lodging of the First Information Report on 25.5.1989 and thereupon starting of the case being Sherpur Case No. 10 dated 25.5.1989 by the respondent No. 3 under Section 6 of the Excise Act is illegal and without lawful authority and the same is liable to be quashed. 

 5. Dr. Kamal Hossain the learned Advocate tor the petitioner has submitted that the proceedings of G.R. Case No. 43(2)89 of the Court of Upazila Magistrate (as then was) Sherpur arising out of Sherpur Police station Case No. 10 dated 25.5.1989 under Section 46 of the Excise Act having been initiated by the person not authorised by the provisions of Excises and Salt Act 1944 and the Rules framed there-under in that under the provision of Excises and Salt Act Police is not authorised to seize manually manufactured cigarettes (Biris) on the allegation of marketing the same without affixing properly valued Bandorol or that upon evading excise duty leviable thereon and thereupon to file criminal case and as such the initiation of the criminal case on the basis of FIR lodged by the respondent No. 3 and continuation thereof i.e. G.R. Case No. 43(2) 89 of the Court of Upazila Magistrate, Sherpur being without lawful authority the proceedings of the said case is liable to quashed. The learned Advocate also submitted that as per provision of Excises and Salt Act 1944 and the Rules framed there-under Police is only authorised to act in aid of the Excise Officer when called and that the Police independent of the Excise Officer is not authorised to enquire into as to whether manually manufactured cigarettes (Biris) marketable on payment of duty being marketed without payment of duty and that on the supposed fact that manually manufactured cigarettes are or were being marketed without payment of duty Police is not authorised to seize the same and to initiate- criminal proceeding and as such initiation of the proceeding i.e. G.R. Case No. 43(2) 89 having been made without lawful authority the proceeding is quite illegal and further that the proceeding i.e. G.R. Case No. 43(2) 89 having been initiated by the unauthorised person the same is liable to be declared illegal. The learned Advocate also submitted that although it is seen from the official reports that the proceeding in question i.e. G.R. Case No. 43 (2) 89 has been initiated under section 46 of the Excise Act, but in fact in the Excise and Salt Act. 1944 there is no section like section 46 and that as the same shows that the proceeding i.e. G.R. Case No. 43 (2)89 has been initiated on the supposed violation of a law which is not in the statute book and that the proceeding as has been initiated without application of mind as to that at all any particular offence has been committed under the provisions of the Excise and Salt Act 1944 by the petitioner No. 1 and his employees and customers the same is liable to be quashed. The learned Advocate further submitted that as the petitioner for manufacturing manually-manufactured cigarettes (Biris) obtained licence under the Excise and Salt Rules. 1944 framed as per provision of section 37 of the Excise and Salt Act 1944 there cannot be any proceeding except for violation of the provisions of the Excise and Salt Act. 1944 and the Rules framed thereunder and that being not the case of the Respondents the initiation and continuation of G.R. Case No. 43(2)89 is quite without jurisdiction and continuation thereof is an abuse of the process of law. The learned Advocate lastly submitted that the proceeding in question appears to have been initiated under section 46 of the Excise Act. 1909 (Bengal Act V of 1909) but then also the proceeding is not maintainable in law in that as per provision of section 46 of the Excise Act 1909 one is liable to be prosecuted for selling intoxicant and that manually manufactured cigarettes (Biris) being undoubtedly not 'intoxicant' ashas been defined in the Act of 1909 as 'liquor or intoxicating drugs'. 

 7. Petitioner No. 1 is engaged in manually manufactured cigarettes (Biris) upon obtaining licence from the appropriate authority under the Excise and Salt Rules. 1944 and marketing the Bids on payment of duty by affixing bandorol of a value appropriate to the rate of duty leviable by the provision of the Excise and Salt Act. 1944 hereinafter mentioned as the Act. It is in the Act that the matter as to evation of duty is to be enquired and investigated by the Excise Officer and that Police and other law enforcing agency should only to help the Excise Officer in the discharge of official duties of the Excise Officer. There is no provision in the Act that the Police of its own is authorised to investigate or to search any premises or to seize any vehicle and the products loaded therein on the supposed apprehension that the same is being sold or marketed or going to sold or marketed without payment of duty and that thereupon to initiate any proceeding as in the instant case the respondent Nos. 3 and 4 have done. The learned Assistant Attorney General could not point out any law authorising the Police to seize articles for the manufacture of which the manufacturer has obtain licence under Excise and Salt Rules 1944 on the supposition that those were being marketed or going to be marketed without payment of duty leviable thereon and thereupon to initiate proceeding in question i.e. G.R. Case No. 43(2)89. 

 8. It may be mentioned that Sherpur P.S. Case No. 10 dated 25.5.1989 was filed under section 46 of the Excise Act. There is no section like 46 in the Excise and Salt Act. 1944; that being so the proceeding so initiated is apparently has been initiated upon referring to a provision of law which is not in the statute book. It seems to us that the Respondents No. 3 and 4 initiated the proceeding under the Excise Act 1909 (Bengal Act V of 1909) but as per provision of the aforesaid section proceeding lies only amongst other in case of selling and manufacturing intoxicant which means "liquor or intoxicating drugs." The manually manufactured cigarettes for the manufacture of which manufacturer obtained licence from the competent authority being neither liquor nor intoxicating drugs initiation of the proceeding under section 46 of the Excise Act. 1909 for supposed marketing of the manually-manufactured cigarettes (Biris) without affixing bandorols of a value appropriate to the rate of duty leviable at that time or that by affixing used bandorols is not maintainable.
